add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.prTitle: Add Client resource type and scopes to authorization schema

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh pr list search on the title (branch 35564-client-authz-schema). Its single commit is the benchmark head 1950a511026d; merged as 7e5540896b (rebase), so merged code equals the benchmark head. Files later moved to admin/fgap/ and authorization/fgap/ (May 2025).

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The V1-only guard in AdminPermissions.registerListener is still there today (now in admin/fgap/AdminPermissions.java), but V2 cleanup was added separately: PR #37984 'Remove permissions and resources when their corresponding objects are deleted' (closes #37242) added AdminPermissionsSchema.removeResourceObject, called from ClientApplicationSynchronizer/GroupSynchronizer/RoleSynchronizer/UserSynchronizer on ClientRemovedEvent etc., gated on V2 being enabled. So under V2 the per-object resources and permissions are no longer orphaned.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 'Fix permissions for view-members and manage-members' (commit b200ab0792) replaced resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) with policyStore.findByResourceType(...) flattened to policy.getResources(), so the method returns the names (client ids) of the per-client resources referenced by permissions instead of the type-level 'Clients' resource. It was later renamed getClientIdsByScope and today delegates to FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator.getIdsByScope with the same policy-based logic.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The findByResource call was rewritten in April 2025 (9f079f7874, then moved into FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator), but a null from getResourceTypeResource still dereferenced (resourceTypeResource.getScopes()). Issue #43331 reported exactly this NPE (500 after disabling realm admin permissions), and PR #43353 'Check FGAP enabled before proceeding with evaluation' added `if (!AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.isAdminPermissionsEnabled(root.realm)) return false;` before the lookup, closing the reachable null case.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: canView() still checks only VIEW today, and PR #38559 (2025-04-02) made that deliberate by removing MANAGE->VIEW transitiveness everywhere. The slow path itself was removed by PR #38396 'Support for partial evaluation for clients': ClientsResource now sets canView = isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm) || auth.clients().canView(), so under FGAP V2 listing always uses the paginated store query with permission filtering pushed into the store.

astra.pergunta: #09: PR #38396 makes ClientsResource use the paginated store query whenever FGAP V2 is enabled (canView = isAdminPermissionsEnabled(realm) || canView()), and PR #38559 later removed MANAGE->VIEW transitiveness. Confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #38396: under FGAP V2 the listing uses the paginated store query with partial evaluation, eliminating the slow path for global-MANAGE-only admins.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38559 '[FGAP] remove transitiveness from auth scopes' replaced `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) return true;` in canView(ClientModel) with an admin-role check followed by hasPermission(client, VIEW). Today canView(client) calls eval.hasPermission(new ClientModelRecord(client), null, VIEW), which evaluates the client's own resource (both specific and all-clients permissions apply) and grants only on a permission for that resource id; ClientsResource listing filters via partial evaluation (PR #38396).

astra.pergunta: #10: PR #38559 replaced `if (canView() || canConfigure(client)) return true` with an admin-role check followed by hasPermission(client, VIEW); today the evaluator evaluates the client's own resource with its resource type. Is the short-circuit bug fixed?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #38559: removing the canView() shortcut forces VIEW evaluation on the specific client, and today's evaluator keeps applying both specific and all-clients permissions to that resource.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The test was renamed ClientResourceTypeEvaluationTest and the weak block (getDefaultClientScopes() and removeDefaultClientScope in one try before any grant) is still there unchanged. But PR #50780 ([CVE-2026-14614] FGAP bypass in client scope assignment) added assertions that fetch the scopes with the full realm admin and call removeDefaultClientScope alone expecting Forbidden, plus testClientScopeAssignmentRequiresManageClientScopes, so the removal permission check is now actually exercised.

astra.pergunta: #11: the weak block (getDefaultClientScopes() then removeDefaultClientScope in one try) is still in testManageOnlyOneClient, but PR #50780 added removal assertions that fetch scopes via the full admin and isolate the remove call, plus testClientScopeAssignmentRequiresManageClientScopes. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Confirmado via PR #50780: the new assertions isolate the removal call and close the coverage gap; the weak block remaining does not make it pendente.

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.
add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #46967 'Fix deny unsupported FGAPv2 token-exchange audience checks' (closes #46718) changed ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo from throwing UnsupportedOperationException to `return false`, explicitly because V1 token exchange audience validation failed with HTTP 500 under FGAP V2. Main today still returns false.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.prTitle: Add comprehensive email validation for blocked users

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head commit 5f8a130277 itself is on discourse/discourse main (compare status 'ahead', behind_by=0), pushed directly on 2013-07-29 (committer date) with no associated pull request (commits/{sha}/pulls empty; PR searches by title and BlockedEmail found nothing). Merged code is identical to the benchmark head.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: After the rename to ScreenedEmail (86647f0a54, 2013-08-14) should_block? still did an exact ScreenedEmail.where(email: email) lookup. Commit 'Emails are case insensitive' (01a68f8cc7, 2014-07-16) added before_save :downcase_email to ScreenedEmail, before_validation :downcase_email to User, and compares se.email.downcase with email.downcase in should_block?. Today's screened_email.rb still downcases on save and canonical() downcases the input, so casing no longer bypasses a block.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: On main today ScreenedEmail.should_block? still calls screened_email.record_match! on a match, and ScreeningModel#record_match! (lib/screening_model.rb) still does self.match_count += 1, sets last_match_at and calls save: a non-atomic read-modify-write run from EmailValidator during validation. The history of screened_email.rb and screening_model.rb after the merge shows no change to this side effect (only refactors, the levenshtein lookup and annotations).

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: The unanchored Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) stayed (later "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})" in PR #3463 and 69ad0358c2, 2015) with no end anchor, so gmail.com.evil.com matched. Commit 'SECURITY: email domain whitelist could be bypassed' (2a22b90538, 2018-01-17) appended $ to the regex, with a spec for email.computers.are.evil.com; today's EmailValidator.email_in_restriction_setting? still uses "@(.+\\.)?(#{domains})$". Subdomain matching (evil.example.com for example.com) is intended behaviour upstream since 2015; the suffix bypass is what was fixed.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.bug: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.reason: The signup logic moved from create_account_controller.js to controllers/signup.js, and kept the 2013 pattern until mid-2025: rejectedEmails.pushObject(result.values.email) on a server email error, and emailValidation failing on rejectedEmails.includes(email). PR #33072 (merged 2025-08-06, ced043be3c) deleted that pushObject block. The PR is mainly about destination_url cookies and does not explain the deletion. On main today, signup.js still declares rejectedEmails and still checks includes(), but nothing adds to the array, so a server rejection can no longer leave a stale client-side block. The separate invite-acceptance controller (invites/show.js, added later) has its own copy of the pattern; that is a different flow and is not counted here.

astra.pergunta: PR #33072 (cookie handling) deleted the rejectedEmails.pushObject block in signup.js. The array and check remain, but nothing populates them. Is this confirmado or descontinuado, and does the same pattern in invites/show.js make it pendente?
astra.resposta: Confirmado. #33072 removed the population of rejectedEmails, which eliminates the reported behaviour in signup. Under the given definition the fix counts even though it is incidental and the PR does not mention the bug. The cache in invites/show.js belongs to another flow and may deserve a separate investigation, but it does not make this case pendente.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.prTitle: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema

prOriginal.nota: Found with gh search prs by title. The PR has a single commit equal to the benchmark head (7355f05e6a); it was merged into main as 679f44692d with the same commit message, so the merged code matches the benchmark head.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The merged GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returned hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). PR #38559 '[FGAP] remove transitiveness from auth scopes' changed it to hasPermission(null, MANAGE). Today's main (fgap/GroupPermissionsV2.java) checks only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE in canManage().

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 'Fix permissions for view-members and manage-members' rewrote getGroupIdsWithViewPermission to iterate the resources of the Groups-type policies and call hasPermission(gr.getName(), ...) and granted.add(gr.getName()), so it passes and returns group ids (resource names) instead of resource ids. The method was later turned into an UnsupportedOperationException in the V2 evaluator refactor.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 replaced resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) with policyStore.findByResourceType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) flattened to policy.getResources(), so per-group resources attached to Groups permissions are enumerated even though they carry no type. The fix does not add a type to the resources, but the missing per-group grants behaviour is gone.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: PR #38015 changed JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery to match the resource name to the bare groupId when admin permissions V2 are enabled for the realm, keeping the 'group.resource.'+groupId pattern only for V1. Members of V2-authorized groups are no longer excluded from the user search filter.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.bug: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.
add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.reason: The evaluator still dereferences the Groups type resource without a null check (61cb0acbc4 on 2025-04-01 dropped the findByResource(null) call, and today FineGrainedAdminPermissionEvaluator.hasPermission calls resourceTypeResource.getScopes() unguarded). But the trigger, an existing admin-permissions client lacking the Groups type resource because AdminPermissionsSchema.init returned early, was fixed by PR #48320 (2026-04-29): init now runs ensureSchemaUpToDate, creating every missing type resource and scope, and MigrateTo26_7_0 runs it for every realm with FGAP. Issue #49732 (2026-06-05) shows the missing Groups resource happened in real upgrades; PR #49893 (2026-06-23) also calls init in MigrateTo26_6_2.

astra.pergunta: Confirmado (via #48320 backfill or #49893 migration fix) or pendente since the evaluator has no null check?
astra.resposta: Confirmado by PR #48320 (2026-04-29): the backfill run by the migration removes the condition that triggered the bug; #49893 complements it on the 26.6.2 migration path but is not the first fix.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.prTitle: Add guest management functionality to existing bookings

prOriginal.nota: Found via the commit history of addGuests.handler.ts (first commit baa9045af7, 'feat: ability to add guests via app.cal.com/bookings (#14740)'). PR headRefOid equals the benchmark head and the merged handler is byte-identical to the benchmark head. The repo calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #17017 changed `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` to `||` in addGuests.handler.ts, so team ADMINs pass the check. The check was later replaced by PermissionCheckService (#24026, fallback OWNER/ADMIN) and is absent today, but the fix came first.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 rewrote the filter to compare `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()` against the lowercased blacklist; today sanitizeAndFilterGuests still does `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(baseGuestEmail)` with the lowercased input, so mixed case no longer bypasses it.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 added a Set-based dedup of input guests by lowercased base email (now deduplicateGuestEmails), so repeated emails in one request are collapsed before createMany.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: Today the handler still reads booking.attendees, filters in memory, then BookingRepository.updateBookingAttendees runs a separate booking.update with attendees.createMany, no transaction or lock. schema.prisma Attendee still has only indexes on email/bookingId, no unique (bookingId,email), so concurrent requests can both insert.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 made the existing-attendee dedup case-insensitive, but validateUserPermissions today still uses `attendee.email === user.email`, so an attendee whose stored email differs in case is still FORBIDDEN. Half of the TP's behaviour remains.

astra.pergunta: Dedup half fixed by #24298, authorization still case-sensitive today; which status for the TP as a whole?
astra.resposta: pendente: partial fix, the authorization still compares case-sensitively and can return FORBIDDEN for a valid attendee, so the defective behaviour still exists.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24298 changed `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` to pass uniqueGuests; today sendGuestNotifications passes uniqueGuestEmails (filtered of existing attendees) as newGuests, so a re-submitted existing attendee no longer gets AttendeeScheduledEmail.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: PR #24414 moved the calendar update into updateCalendarEvent, building EventManager from `...booking.user` with getUsersCredentialsIncludeServiceAccountKey(booking.user) instead of ctx.user, so the organizer's credentials are used. Still so today.

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.bug: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.
add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.reason: The flow is unchanged today: guests are persisted via updateBookingAttendees, then `await updateCalendarEvent(booking, evt)` runs with no try/catch in the handler, and EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees still just awaits updateAllCalendarEvents (which keeps its internal try/catch). No upstream change touched this ordering or error handling.

prOriginal.nota: Found by title with gh pr list (branch jguer/add-anon-device-limit). Its last commit is the benchmark head bbd8c507; squash-merged as 3647ba73 on 2023-12-12, and database.go, impl.go and client.go at the merge commit are byte-identical to the benchmark head. anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: On main, AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice (anonstore/database.go) still calls CountDevices and, if count < deviceLimit, runs the INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert in a separate WithDbSession call, with no transaction, lock or conditional insert. The file's later commits (#80028 pagination, Spanner support/removal, lint) never touched the check-then-insert sequence, so concurrent new devices can still all pass the count check.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: TagDevice in anonimpl/impl.go on main still takes X-Grafana-Device-Id verbatim from the request and tagDeviceUI admits every new ID until the store reports ErrDeviceLimitReached, after which client.go rejects authentication. The validator added in #94700 (AnonUserLimitValidator, a no-op fake in OSS) and the cache change in #94218 do not validate device IDs or rate-limit creation per client, so slots can still be exhausted with fabricated IDs.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit on main (anonstore/database_test.go) is unchanged: it admits one device, swaps to a new ID and asserts ErrDeviceLimitReached, never updating an existing device at the limit. The later TestIntegrationAnonDeviceService_DeviceLimitWithCache (impl_test.go, #94218) repeats the admitted device1 only through the local-cache hit, so the store's updateDevice path at capacity is still not exercised by any test.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: PR #94218 'Anonymous: Fix anonymous cache ignoring device limit evaluation' changed tagDeviceUI so that on ErrDeviceLimitReached the cache entry is set to false and later cache hits with false return ErrDeviceLimitReached; any other store error now deletes the cache entry. A rejected device can no longer authenticate through the cache-hit branch; main still has this code and a test for it.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: The merged PR #79265 did not add device_limit to conf/defaults.ini. Six days later PR #79494 'Anonymous: Add device limits to stats' added 'device_limit =' under [auth.anonymous] in conf/defaults.ini, so the key exists in the loaded INI and GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT can override it; the key is still there on main.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.bug: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.
anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.reason: On main, TagDevice still begins with 'if deviceID == "" { return nil }', and Anonymous.Authenticate in client.go only fails on ErrDeviceLimitReached, otherwise returning an anonymous identity. prOriginal.nota: Found via gh api commits/<head>/pulls; PR headRefOid equals the benchmark head 820d7fa87e; merge commit e043a5efd8 has an identical diff. calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy (same history).

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.bug: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.reason: PR #10157 'fix: replace all async foreach callbacks' replaced the forEach(async ...) loops in vital/lib/reschedule.ts, wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and the trpc requestReschedule handler (where bookings.tsx's reschedule moved) with map(async ...) plus await Promise.all / Promise.allSettled, so getCalendar failures are awaited and caught. Today both reschedule.ts files still use const promises = bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) followed by await Promise.all(promises) inside try/catch.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.bug: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.prTitle: Enhance embed URL handling and validation system

prOriginal.nota: Benchmark head 4f8aed2 is itself on upstream main: direct commit by Robin Ward, 2013-12-31 ('FEATURE: Embeddable Discourse comments, now with simple-rss instead of feedzirra'), no PR associated (gh commits/<sha>/pulls empty). Base 62db063 is the revert of the earlier attempt; diff identical to the benchmark.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: embed.js moved to public/javascripts/embed.js (2013-12-31) and was rewritten many times, but postMessageReceived on main still accepts any message whose origin is a substring of the Discourse URL: `if (!normalizeUrl(DE.discourseUrl).includes(normalizeUrl(e.origin))) return;` (indexOf became includes in #17541). The substring origin check that lets a prefix origin set the iframe height is unchanged.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The SiteSetting comparisons were replaced by EmbeddableHost.record_for_url on 2015-08-18 (d1c69189, `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), which fixed a mixed-case admin host but still did not downcase the incoming URI host. PR #17840 made UrlHelper.escape_uri/normalized_encode (used by record_for_url and url_allowed?) downcase the host via normalize_with_ruby_uri, so both referer and embed_url checks are case-insensitive on main today.

astra.pergunta: #04: confirmado at 2015-08-18 (EmbeddableHost where lower(host)=?, incoming host not downcased) or 2022-08-09 (PR #17840 normalize_with_ruby_uri downcases incoming host)?
astra.resposta: Confirmado at PR #17840, 2022-08-09: it lowercases the incoming host; after 2015 an uppercase URL host still failed.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Two days after the original commit, ed2e53bb ('FIX: Support feeds with description as well as content') replaced `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with `content = i.content || i.description; if content ... end`, removing the nil.scrub crash. PollFeed was later moved to the rss-polling plugin (#8233).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Post#cook on main still does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and TopicEmbed.import still defaults cook_method to raw_html (unless embed_support_markdown). RSS import moved to plugins/discourse-rss-polling (#8233), whose FeedItem#cook_method returns nil for HTML items, so feed HTML is still stored as cooked without sanitization; the only PrettyText.sanitize added (#42808, 2026-08-25) is on the expansion path, not the stored post.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The nil-contents part was fixed on 2015-05-06 (edae9d7a, `contents ||= ''`, today `contents.to_s`). The unescaped URL in the 'imported from' link survived the move into imported_from_html until PR #42314 ('SECURITY: Escape embed URL for HTML attribute context in footer'), which applies ERB::Util.html_escape after URL normalization; that matches the injection described.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: TopicEmbed.import on main still does an unlocked topic_embed_by_url lookup and then creates the post/embed inside Topic.transaction with no mutex and no rescue of the unique violation; fb8ba5e1 (2015-06-15) only added validates_uniqueness_of (application-level, not race-safe). The synchronous PollFeed inside TopicRetriever was removed with #8233, but the scheduled RSS plugin import and RetrieveTopic/import_remote can still race on the same URL.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 5fb962a6 ('in the case that an imported post was deleted, don't error out of the PollFeed job') changed the update guard to `if post && content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`, followed the same day by a post.topic check. Main today returns early with `return post unless post&.topic`.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: Nil contents was handled on 2015-05-06 (edae9d7a). find_remote began rescuing OpenURI::HTTPError on 2017-05-25 (39e19481, then Net::OpenTimeout on 2017-08-10), but import_remote then dereferenced the nil response; PR #5200 added `return if response.nil?` in import_remote, so a dead URL no longer raises. Main keeps both guards.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: PR #14975 ('FIX: Convert URLs embedded topics to absolute form') replaced the start_with?('/') + sub(/^\/+/) rewrite in absolutize_urls with `URI.join(prefix, href)`, which keeps protocol-relative URLs on their own host and resolves path-relative ones (spec changed to images/wat.jpg). Main is unchanged since.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: best.html.erb was replaced by EmbedHelper#embed_post_date; PR #28014 (2024-07-22) switched to `dt.strftime I18n.t("datetime_formats.formats.short_no_year")`, which localizes the order, but Ruby strftime %B is not locale-aware and the locale formats use %B (e.g. de '%-d. %B'), so month names still come out in English on main.

astra.pergunta: #24: PR #28014 (2024-07-22) switched to strftime with I18n format strings; %B/%b still English in Ruby strftime. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Pendente: #28014 localizes the format order only; month names still come out in English.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: disqus.thor moved to script/import_scripts/disqus.rb (efff3351, 2015-07-01) still calling import_remote with the title only. 72d7c055 (2016-08-17) added a hard-coded IMPORT_CATEGORY and a rescue of OpenURI::HTTPError, but on main the thread's created_at is still never applied to the topic or first post, so imported topics still get the import date.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 67e20416 ('Prevent topic_retriever from retrieving more than once a minute') changed the throttle key from per-URL `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` to the global `retrieved_topic`, so different unknown articles can no longer each trigger a full synchronous feed poll. The synchronous PollFeed call was later removed entirely with #8233 (2019-11-12).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: spec/requests/embed_controller_spec.rb on main still has 'is 404 without an embed_url' doing `get "/embed/comments"` with no embeddable host and asserting only the generic embed.error body. The controller now rejects via `EmbeddableHost.url_allowed?(embed_url)`, which fails for a missing host and a missing URL alike, so the example still cannot detect a missing embed_url check.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: On 2014-04-24 (#2428) the embed_by_username guard and its spec were removed, while 'requires feed_polling_url' kept feed_polling_enabled false and stayed gappy. spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb and Jobs::PollFeed were deleted from core by #8233 (RSS polling moved to a plugin) without a change targeting the gap.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: The same day, cab6a3f3 ('Don't forget to precompile the embed css') added 'embed.css' to config.assets.precompile, and 5621a645 moved embed.js from app/assets to public/javascripts so it is served statically without precompilation.

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.bug: The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.
enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.reason: 67e20416 replaced the per-URL throttle key with a global `retrieved_topic` 60s key; main's TopicRetriever is identical, so varying the query string no longer bypasses the throttle (at most one anonymous retrieval per minute site-wide). feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.prTitle: FEATURE: Can edit category/host relationships for embedding

prOriginal.nota: No upstream PR: the benchmark head d1c69189 is itself a direct commit by Robin Ward on discourse/discourse main (committer date 2015-08-20, no associated pull request; gh pr search by title finds nothing), and it is an ancestor of main. The reference date is that commit's date.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: app/models/embeddable_host.rb on main still has 'before_validation do host.sub!(%r{\Ahttps?://}, ""); host.sub!(%r{/.*\z}, "") end' with no nil guard, and Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host still assigns params[:embeddable_host][:host] directly. Later commits only reformatted the regexes (\A/\z, RedundantSelf); a request without host still raises NoMethodError.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: On main, Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy still do EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call save_host(host, :update) / host.destroy without a nil check or find/raise. The controller gained tags, user and staff logging but the lookups are unchanged, so an unknown id still yields NoMethodError (500).

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: record_for_host became record_for_url and still runs where("lower(host) = ?", host) without lowercasing the bound value. Since PR #17840 (2022-08-09, onebox URL normalization) UrlHelper.normalized_encode downcases the host when the URL parses with ::URI, which covers ordinary ASCII URLs, but URLs that fall back to Addressable (e.g. non-ASCII path) keep the host's case, so the mismatch is only partly gone.

astra.pergunta: Lookup still compares lower(host) to an un-lowercased URI host; #17840 made normalized_encode downcase the host on the ::URI path, with an Addressable fallback. Confirmado, pendente or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #17840 is a partial fix: the Addressable fallback keeps ASCII host case (IDNA only for non-ASCII hosts), e.g. https://ExAmPlE.com/café still binds ExAmPlE.com; its onebox motivation would not prevent counting it as a fix if it removed the behaviour.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Two days after the merge, commit d418c4cf (2015-08-22, 'FIX: Bug with migrating old embeddedable hosts with http://') added migration FixMigratedHosts that strips ^https?:// from embeddable_hosts.host, which fixes migrated hosts with a scheme. Nothing ever stripped path segments from migrated rows, and the original migration still inserts the lines verbatim, so migrated hosts with a path still never match URI.host; partial fix only.

astra.pergunta: d418c4cf strips only the scheme from migrated hosts, not paths. Confirmado or pendente?
astra.resposta: Partial fix: example.com/path stays unmatched; the bug explicitly includes path segments, so being uncommon does not remove the residual case. Would be confirmado if the report were scheme-only.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb on main still executes "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)" with each legacy host interpolated unescaped. Later commits on the file (Rails 5 fixes, formatting, the 2026 uncategorized guard) left the interpolation as is.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Fourteen minutes after the feature commit, Robin Ward pushed 676416f4 'FIX: Build broken when someone didn't have an embed category', which keeps category_id = 0 and only reads category_row[0]['id'] if category_row.cmd_tuples > 0, falling back to uncategorized_category_id. Main still has that guard (and since #39971 also guards the uncategorized lookup).

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: The post-save overwrite with Category.findById(categoryId) survived #14517 (2021, which only set the initial category with an uncategorized fallback) and #26374. PR #26420 bound the chooser to this.category, saved props.category_id = this.category.id and deleted the findById(this.categoryId) line, so a new host keeps the uncategorized category initialised in init after saving; #30122 (2025) later moved editing to a separate form page.

astra.pergunta: Overwrite with findById(categoryId) after save removed in #26420 (DEV refactor of CategoryChooser); #14517 only fixed initial render; #30122 later rewrote the UI. Confirmado or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #14517 kept the line that cleared the category after saving; #26420 resolved the described behaviour even though tagged DEV; the later #30122 rewrite does not make it descontinuado since it was already fixed.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: Commit bf9626d0 'FIX: Embedding was broken with non-english URLs and ports' added 'host << ":#{uri.port}" if uri.port.present? && uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443' in record_for_url before the lookup, so a stored host:port now matches. The line is still on main and spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb has an 'it works with ports' case.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.bug: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.
feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.reason: The 2-5 letter TLD limit in EmbeddableHost's host regex was widened in steps: 436da215ae (2015-12-15, 'allow .network') to {2,7}, then PR #4816 (2017-04-15, 'increase host_must_be_valid regex for .technology TLD') to {2,10}, which is the first change that accepts the bug's example example.technology; PR #7948 (2019-07-26) raised it to {2,24}. Today's main still has `\.[a-z]{2,24}` in host_must_be_valid. Fix date taken as #4816 because it makes the cited case pass; the partial widening started 2015-12-15.

prOriginal.nota: Found via gh search prs 'Localization fallbacks'. Merged with a regular merge: the benchmark head ecfa17b5 is the 2nd of 7 PR commits and is on upstream history. feature-localization-fallbacks-server-si.reason: PR #3786 'FIX: Load fallback locales in Sidekiq jobs' added I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! right after I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale in Jobs::Base#perform, so jobs (and the mailers they run) load the fallback catalogs. feature-localization-fallbacks-server-si.bug: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.
feature-localization-fallbacks-server-si.reason: The cache key in translate_no_override is still key+locale+backend id today, but commit ec2f3169 ('FIX: Using the default_locale in locale fallbacks caused problems', citing multisite missing translations) removed SiteSetting.default_locale from FallbackLocaleList; the chain is now locale, its static LocaleSiteSetting.fallback_locale chain, then :en, so cached fallback results no longer depend on any site setting. The dependency had been dropped by the 2015-11-13 refactor 3720783 and re-added on 2018-01-22 (ce060e2) before this final removal.

astra.pergunta: confirmado by ec2f3169 (2020-05-06) or descontinuado (3720783 refactor 2015 / ec2f3169)?
astra.resposta: confirmado - ec2f3169 deliberately removed site-dependent default_locale fallbacks, eliminating the mismatch; the 2015 refactor was only temporary since the behaviour returned in 2018.

For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: The next/previous paging that set offset and called findMembers (which unconditionally setProperties from each response) survived unchanged, last in components/group-members-input rendered by admin/templates/group.hbs. No change ever added request cancellation or a staleness check; the admin group pages that rendered this paging were removed in c82b2dcc 'Remove admin group management pages' (2018-04-09), and the component itself was deleted as dead code in 352d43b1 (#8356, 2019-11-18), with findMembers rewritten to append-only load-more.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: Commit 8fd69fd3 'FIX: group member pages only showing first 50 members alphabetically' (2015-02-19) added a group/members controller with a loadMore action and a LoadMore view mixin on the public group members page, so members beyond the first 50 page are fetched by infinite scroll.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: Commit e8323fa5 'FIX: removing a group from a user was not removing primary group' (2015-02-09) made remove_member load the user, set primary_group_id = nil when it equals the group id and save it, with a spec asserting primary_group_id becomes nil.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: Admin add_members pushes every username into group.users without skipping existing members, so adding someone already in the group hits the unique group_users index, returns a 500 and leaves earlier users partially added.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: PR #3378 'FIX: show error message if user already exist in group' (merged 2015-04-15) wrapped group.add in if !group.users.include?(user) and returns a 422 member_already_exist error instead of hitting the unique index (spec 'returns 422 if member already exists'). astra.pergunta: Does #3378 (skip-check returning 422 for an existing member, partial add still possible) count as the fix, or should the later all-or-nothing pre-check be the fix date?
astra.resposta: confirmado by 499bed69/#3378 on 2015-04-15: it directly fixed adding an existing member (no unique-index violation, 422 instead of 500); the partial add is a residual problem fixed later and does not delay the classification.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.bug: The public group members endpoint takes `limit` from params with no upper bound or positivity check, letting a visitor request huge pages or trigger a 500 with a negative limit.
fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.reason: GroupsController#members got a negative check in 982df3c1 'FIX: return status 400 for invalid member params' (2018-06-29: limit < 0 raises InvalidParameters) and an upper bound in 704c5795 'FIX: do not allow unbound membership lookups' (2019-06-17: limit > 1000 raises InvalidParameters). oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: The merged code (kept by the 2023-09-20 re-add #11453) set the placeholder unconditionally. #11862 restricted it to credential-sync mode (`&& credentialSyncingEnabled`), so normal refreshes no longer overwrite the real token; that code is unchanged today, and Office365 later moved to OAuthManager.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: #11059 was reverted the same day (#11450) and re-added next day by #11453 'with proper handling of safeParse'. oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: zoho-bigin/lib/CrmService.ts (renamed from CalendarService.ts in #14272) still does `const credentialId = credential.id` and passes credentialId as the userId argument of refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId), which serializes it as calcomUserId.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: #11508 'fix: Salesforce by wrapping the refresh logic in a try/catch' replaced `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw` with `if (!response.ok)`; today's CrmService.ts still checks response.ok. The stale-token part is tracked as #17.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: Until #27264 the Connection was built from credentialKey.access_token/instance_url after persisting the refreshed token. #27264 assigns credentialKey.access_token (and this.accessToken/instanceUrl) from the refresh result before building the Connection; credentialKey.instance_url is still not reassigned (minor residual).

astra.pergunta: Did #27264 fix jsforce.Connection being built with pre-refresh credentialKey tokens?
astra.resposta: Yes; after a successful refresh credentialKey.access_token is reassigned before building the Connection; instance_url not reassigned is a minor residual.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.bug: The app-credential webhook looks up appStoreMetadata by app.slug, but the map is keyed by dirName, so apps whose slug differs from their directory (e.g. google-calendar) always get a 404 and their credentials cannot be synced.
oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.reason: #11530 'fix: credential sync app lookup' changed the select to dirName and indexes appStoreMetadata[app.dirName]; today's route.ts keeps that lookup.

prOriginal.nota: Found by head branch ref/spans-evict-oldest; its last commit is the benchmark head eb9623b4, merged as 74618671 at 2025-06-02T10:06Z. The whole change was reverted the same day by #92626 (14:50Z) for a 30% insert overhead.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 restored SET keys and sunionstore, removing the zunionstore calls with default SUM, without targeting this bug. A later separate PR (#94033, 2025-06-23) reintroduced zunionstore with default SUM under span-buf:z:, but today's add-buffer.lua has no ZSET at all (SET member keys, after the ZSET cleanup #107863).

astra.pergunta: PR #92393 was reverted the same day by #92626 for 30% insert overhead (restores SET/sunionstore, removes zpopmin, restores 10000 loop); #94033 (2025-06-23) later reintroduced ZSET under span-buf:z: with zunionstore/zpopmin, and today add-buffer.lua uses SETs with no ZSET. Which status for #03?
astra.resposta: The revert removed ZSET/ZUNIONSTORE and so the score-summing mechanism, without a targeted fix; reintroduction in #94033 is to be judged separately.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: PR #92617 'fix(spans): Rename span buf prefix' (2025-06-02, 1.5 h after the merge) states it fixes a regression in #92393 where the key data type changed without renaming the keys, and moves all keys to the sb: namespace, removing the WRONGTYPE collision with old SET keys. optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.bug: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.
optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 removed the zpopmin eviction from add-buffer.lua, so the root span could no longer be evicted while the has-root flag stayed set; the revert was for performance, not this bug. Today's script has no zpopmin; segment size is limited by detaching subsegments by byte count instead.

astra.pergunta: PR #92393 was reverted the same day by #92626 for 30% insert overhead (restores SET/sunionstore, removes zpopmin, restores 10000 loop); #94033 (2025-06-23) later reintroduced ZSET under span-buf:z: with zunionstore/zpopmin, and today add-buffer.lua uses SETs with no ZSET. astra.resposta: The revert removed zpopmin, ending that eviction path without specifically fixing its relation to has-root.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.reason: The revert #92626 restored `for i = 0, 10000 do` as part of withdrawing the whole implementation for performance reasons. Today's loop is `for i = 0, 100 do` in a different, rewritten implementation, which does not carry the original change.

prOriginal.nota: PR 'ref(span-buffer): Introduce multiprocessed flusher' (branch spans-buffer-multiprocessing); its last commit is the benchmark head 3162ad68. Squash commit 9bf83b05 on master has no diff from the head under src/sentry/spans, src/sentry/consumers and tests/sentry/spans.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: _ensure_processes_alive kept `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` until PR #115050 'fix(span-buffer): Fix another process leak' (merged 2026-05-07) changed it to isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess), which SpawnProcess satisfies. Master today has the BaseProcess check before kill().

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: join() kept the `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before terminate() until PR #114955 'fix(span-buffer): Fix flusher processes leaking on timeout' (merged 2026-05-06) removed the break and kills every process, with a test that reproduces the early break on timeout. Master today loops over all processes and calls kill() on each.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: SpanFlusher.__init__ on master still sets self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards), and --flusher-processes is still a plain click int option (default 1) forwarded by factory.py without validation, so 0 still becomes one process per shard.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.bug: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.
span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.reason: submit() on master still loops `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, and SpansBuffer.get_memory_info still returns iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client) where every buffer's client is the same get_redis_client() cluster. The cluster-wide INFO is still repeated once per flusher process buffer.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.bug: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
unified-storage-performance-optimization.reason: After #97529 getOrCreateIndex did GetIndex then build with a '// TODO??? We want to block while building the index ... for the same key' comment and no dedupe, while BuildIndex only locked the final cache assignment. PR #107886 added a singleflight.Group (buildIndex.Do keyed by key.String()) with a recheck of GetIndex inside, so concurrent callers for the same key share one build. Today getOrCreateIndex still uses s.buildIndex.DoChan with the recheck.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.bug: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
unified-storage-performance-optimization.reason: TotalDocs kept ranging over the plain b.cache map without cacheMu until PR #106842 replaced the map+RWMutex with localcache.CacheService and TotalDocs iterated b.cache.Items(), a copy taken under the cache's lock, removing the unsynchronized map read. The PR targeted a TTL cache, not the race, but the TotalDocs loop survived and became safe. Today TotalDocs iterates GetOpenIndexes() (keys copied under cacheMx.RLock) and getCachedIndex (RLock), so the race is still gone.

astra.pergunta: TotalDocs race became safe via #106842 (map -> mutex-protected localcache, Items() copy), a change targeting TTL caching, not the bug: confirmado or descontinuado?
astra.resposta: #106842 fixed the behaviour by replacing the map with a mutex-protected cache whose Items() returns a copy under lock; by the definition any way of fixing counts even without intent, so not descontinuado; the later return to a locked map does not change the milestone.
